title.raw: 卷52 趙逸 胡方回 胡叟 宋繇 張湛 宗欽 段承根 闞駰 劉昞 趙柔 索敞 陰仲達 Volume 56: Zhao Yi, Hu Fanghui, Hu Sou, Song Yao, Zhang Zhan, Zong Qin, Duan Chenggen, Kai Yin, Liu Bing, Zhao Rou, Sou Chang, Yin Zhongda

sentences.zh: 趙逸 胡方回 胡叟 宋繇 張湛 宗欽 段承根 闞駰 劉昞 趙柔 索敞 陰仲達

translations.literal: Zhao Yi; Hu Fanghui; Hu Sou; Song Yao; Zhang Zhan; Zong Qin; Duan Chenggen; Yan Yin; Liu Bing; Zhao Rou; Suo Chang; Yin Zhongda
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi, and hu Fanghui, and hu Sou, and song Yao, and zhang Zhan, and zong Qin, and duan Chenggen, and yan Yin, and liu Bing, and zhao Rou, and suo Chang, and yin Zhongda

translations.literal: Zhao Yi, courtesy name Siqun, was a native of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi, whose courtesy name was Siqun, came from Tianshui.

translations.literal: His tenth-generation ancestor Rong was Han Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His tenth-generation ancestor Rong had served the Han as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

translations.literal: His father Chang was Yellow Gate Attendant under Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chang had been a Yellow Gate Attendant under Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 逸好學夙成，仕姚興，歷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Yi loved learning and matured early in scholarship; he served Yao Xing and successively held the post of Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yi took to scholarship from youth and mastered it early; he entered the service of Yao Xing and rose to Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 為興將齊難軍司，征赫連屈丐。

translations.literal: He served as army aide to Yao Xing's general Qi Nan in the campaign against Helian Qugai.
translations.idiomatic: He served as army aide to Yao Xing's general Qi Nan in the campaign against Helian Qugai.

sentences.zh: 難敗，為屈丐所虜，拜著作郎。

translations.literal: Nan was defeated and Yi was captured by Qugai, who appointed him Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Nan was defeated, Yi was taken captive by Qugai and appointed Drafting Secretary.

sentences.zh: 世祖平統萬，見逸所著，曰：「此豎無道，安得為此言乎！

translations.literal: When the Emperor Shizu pacified Tongwan, he saw what Yi had written and said, "How can this scoundrel, who is utterly without the Way, presume to write such words!
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu pacified Tongwan, he came upon Yi's writings and exclaimed, "This villain is utterly lawless—how dare he write such things!

translations.literal: Who is the author?
translations.idiomatic: Who wrote this?

translations.literal: Bring him forward at once.
translations.idiomatic: Have him brought forward at once.

sentences.zh: 」司徒崔浩進曰：「彼之謬述，亦猶子雲之美新，皇王之道，固宜容之。

translations.literal: " Minister over the Masses Cui Hao stepped forward and said, "His mistaken writings are like Yang Xiong's Mei Xin— the way of emperors and kings should indeed make room for such things.
translations.idiomatic: " Minister over the Masses Cui Hao stepped forward and said, "His misguided writings are like Yang Xiong's Mei Xin— the way of sage-kings should make room even for that.

translations.literal: " The emperor then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then let the matter drop.

translations.literal: Yi was appointed Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 神䴥三年三月上巳，帝幸白虎殿，命百僚賦詩，逸製詩序，時稱為善。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shenyu, on the third-month shangsi festival, the emperor visited the White Tiger Hall, ordered the hundred officials to compose poems, and Yi drafted the preface to the poems; at the time it was praised as excellent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shenyu, on the third-month shangsi festival, the emperor visited the White Tiger Hall and ordered the hundred officials to compose poems; Yi drafted the preface, which was then widely praised.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜寧朔將軍、赤城鎮將，綏和荒服，十有餘年，百姓安之。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and garrison commander of Chicheng; for more than ten years he soothed and harmonized the frontier regions, and the common people lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and garrison commander of Chicheng; for more than ten years he brought calm to the frontier, and the people lived securely under him.

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized begging to be relieved; only after a long while was his request granted.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly petitioned to be relieved of office, and only after a long delay was he allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 性好墳素，白首彌勤，年踰七十，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: By nature he loved the classics; in white-haired old age he grew only more diligent, and past seventy he never laid book from hand.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the classics by nature; in old age he grew only more assiduous, and past seventy he still never set a book down.

sentences.zh: 凡所著述，詩、賦、銘、頌，五十餘篇。

translations.literal: In all, the works he composed— poems, rhapsodies, inscriptions, and eulogies— numbered more than fifty pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Everything he wrote— poems, rhapsodies, inscriptions, and eulogies— came to more than fifty pieces.

translations.literal: Yi's elder brother Wen, courtesy name Sigong.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's elder brother Wen, whose courtesy name was Sigong.

sentences.zh: 博學有高名，姚泓天水太守。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and of high reputation, he was Tianshui Administrator under Yao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned and highly regarded, and served as Tianshui Administrator under Yao Hong.

translations.literal: When Liu Yu destroyed Hong, Wen fell into Di hands.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu destroyed Yao Hong, Wen fell into Di hands.

sentences.zh: 氐王楊盛，盛子難當，既有漢中，以溫為輔國將軍、秦梁二州刺史。

translations.literal: The Di king Yang Sheng and Sheng's son Yang Dang, once they held Hanzhong, appointed Wen General Who Assists the State and governor of Qin and Liang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The Di king Yang Sheng and his son Yang Dang, once they held Hanzhong, made Wen General Who Assists the State and governor of Qin and Liang.

sentences.zh: 及難當稱蕃，世祖以溫為難當府司馬。

translations.literal: When Dang declared himself a vassal, Emperor Shizu appointed Wen staff officer in Dang's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Dang submitted as a vassal, Emperor Shizu appointed Wen staff officer in Dang's headquarters.

translations.literal: He died at Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, He died at Chouchi.

translations.literal: His eldest son Guangxia was a Secretariat Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Guangxia served as a Secretariat Erudite.

translations.literal: His third son was Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The third son was Yan.

translations.literal: His account is given in the Biographies of Filial Sons.
translations.idiomatic: His story is told in the Biographies of Filial Sons.

sentences.zh: 初，姚萇以逸伯父遷為尚書左僕射，卒于長安。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yao Chang had appointed Yi's father's elder brother Qian Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Qian died at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yao Chang had appointed Yi's father's elder brother Qian Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and qian died at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 劉裕滅姚泓，徙遷子孫於建業。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu destroyed Yao Hong, Hong's descendants of the Qian line were moved to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu destroyed Yao Hong, the descendants of the Qian line were relocated to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 遷玄孫翼、翼從子超宗、令勝、遐、叔隆、穆等，太和、景明中，相尋歸降。

translations.literal: Qian's great-great-grandson Yi, Yi's grandnephew Chaozong, Ling Sheng, Xia, Shulong, Mu, and others successively submitted in surrender during the Taihe and Jingming reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's great-great-grandson Yi, Yi's grandnephew Chaozong, Ling Sheng, Xia, Shulong, Mu, and others came over in surrender one after another during the Taihe and Jingming reigns.

sentences.zh: 翼，粗涉書傳，通率有器藝。

translations.literal: Yi had rough acquaintance with written tradition and was open and forthright, with capacity and skill.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had a rough grounding in the classics and was open and forthright, with real talent and ability.

sentences.zh: 初為平昌太守，甚有治稱。

translations.literal: At first he was Administrator of Pingchang, with a strong reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as Administrator of Pingchang, where he won a strong reputation for good governance.

sentences.zh: 入歷軍校，加鎮遠將軍長史，深為領軍元叉所知待。

translations.literal: He entered service in the army schools, was made chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the Distant, and was deeply known and favored by the Commander-in-Chief Yuan Cha.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the army schools, became chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the Distant, and won the deep trust of Commander-in-Chief Yuan Cha.

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously awarded General of the Left and Governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made General of the Left and Governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 超宗，身長八尺，頗有將略。

translations.literal: Chaozong was eight feet in height and had considerable military talent.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong stood eight feet tall and showed considerable military talent.

sentences.zh: 太和末，為豫州平南府長史，帶汝南太守，加建威將軍，賜爵尋陽伯。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taihe reign he was chief clerk in the Pacify-the-South headquarters of Yu Province, concurrently Administrator of Runan, with the additional title General Who Establishes Might, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Taihe he was chief clerk in the Pacify-the-South headquarters of Yu Province and concurrently Administrator of Runan, with the additional title General Who Establishes Might; he was enfeoffed Baron of Xunyang.

translations.literal: He entered court as General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, He entered court as General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 超宗在汝南，多所受納，貨賂太傅北海王詳，詳言之於世宗，除持節、征虜將軍、岐州刺史。

translations.literal: While Chaozong was in Runan he took many bribes; he presented gifts to the Grand Tutor Prince Xiang of Beihai, and Xiang spoke of him to Emperor Shizong, who appointed him Bearer of the Staff, General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and Governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Runan Chaozong took many bribes and curried favor with Grand Tutor Prince Xiang of Beihai; Xiang commended him to Emperor Shizong, who appointed him Bearer of the Staff, General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and Governor of Qi Province.

translations.literal: He was moved to Administrator of Hedong and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Administrator of Hedong and died in office.

sentences.zh: 超宗在河東，更自修厲，清靖愛民，百姓追思之。

translations.literal: In Hedong Chaozong again disciplined himself, was pure, quiet, and loving toward the people, and the common people long remembered him.
translations.idiomatic: In Hedong he disciplined himself anew, governed with purity and care for the people, and the common people long remembered him.

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍、華州刺史，諡曰成伯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded his former rank of general and made Governor of Hua Province, with the posthumous title Baron Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given his former rank of general and made Governor of Hua Province, with the posthumous title Baron Cheng.

translations.literal: His son Yi inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi inherited the title.

translations.literal: He successively served as Outer Court Attendant and Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Outer Court Attendant and Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 超宗弟令勝，亦長八尺，疏狂有膂力。

translations.literal: Chaozong's younger brother Ling Sheng was also eight feet tall, coarse and wild, with great physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong's younger brother Ling Sheng was also eight feet tall— coarse, reckless, and powerfully built.

sentences.zh: 歷河北、恒農二郡太守，並坐貪暴，為御史所彈，遇赦免。

translations.literal: He served as Administrator of Hebei and Hengnong, and in both posts was impeached by the censorate for greed and cruelty; he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He held the prefectures of Hebei and Hengnong, and in both was impeached by the censorate for greed and cruelty, then pardoned.

sentences.zh: 神龜末，自後將軍、太中大夫出為恒農太守，卒官。

translations.literal: At the end of the Shengui reign he left his post as Rear General and Grand Master of Palace Counsel to become Administrator of Hengnong, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Shengui he went out from Rear General and Grand Master of Palace Counsel to become Administrator of Hengnong and died in office.

sentences.zh: 令勝寵惑妾潘，離棄其妻羊氏，夫妻相訟，迭發陰私，醜穢之事，彰於朝野。

translations.literal: Ling Sheng was infatuated with his concubine Pan, cast off his wife the Lady Yang, and husband and wife sued each other back and forth, airing private scandals until the filth of it was known throughout court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Sheng doted on his concubine Pan, abandoned his wife Lady Yang, and the couple sued each other in turn, airing private scandals until the whole affair was notorious at court and in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 遐，初為軍主，從高祖征南陽。

translations.literal: Xia, at first an army commander, followed Emperor Gaozu on the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Xia first served as an army commander and followed Emperor Gaozu on the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 景明初，為梁城戍主，被蕭衍將攻圍。

translations.literal: In the early Jingming reign he was garrison commander of Liangcheng and was besieged by a Liang general.
translations.idiomatic: In early Jingming he was garrison commander of Liangcheng and was besieged by a Liang general.

sentences.zh: 以固守及戰功，封牟平縣開國子，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: For his stout defense and battle merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Mouping with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his stout defense and battle merit he was enfeoffed Viscount of Mouping with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後以左軍將軍、假征虜將軍、督巴東諸軍事，鎮南鄭。

translations.literal: Later he was made General of the Left, acting General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and overseer of all Ba-Dong military affairs, garrisoning Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made General of the Left, acting General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and overseer of all Ba-Dong military affairs, with his seat at Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 時蕭衍冠軍將軍、軍主姜脩眾二萬屯羊口，輔國將軍姜白龍據南城，龍驤將軍泉建率土民北入桑坯，姜脩又分軍據興勢，龍驤將軍譚思文據夾石，司州刺史王僧炳頓南安，並扇動夷獠，規翻南鄭。

translations.literal: At that time the Liang champion general and army commander Jiang Xiu had twenty thousand men encamped at Yangkou; the State-supporting General Jiang Bailong held the southern city; the Dragon-cavalry General Quan Jian led local people north into Sangpi; Jiang Xiu also divided his army to hold Xingshi; the Dragon-cavalry General Tan Siwen held Jiashi; the provincial inspector Wang Sengbing halted at Nan'an— all stirring the Yi and Liao peoples and plotting to turn Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Liang champion general Jiang Xiu had twenty thousand men at Yangkou; Jiang Bailong held the southern city; Quan Jian led locals north into Sangpi; Jiang Xiu also detached forces for Xingshi; Tan Siwen held Jiashi; Wang Sengbing was at Nan'an— all stirring the frontier peoples and plotting to recover Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 遐率甲士九千，所在衝擊，數百里中，莫不摧靡，前後斬首五千餘級。

translations.literal: Xia led nine thousand armored soldiers and struck wherever he went; for several hundred li none could withstand him, and in all he cut off more than five thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Xia led nine thousand armored men and struck wherever he went; for several hundred li nothing stood before him, and he took more than five thousand heads in all.

sentences.zh: 還，以輔國將軍出為滎陽太守。

translations.literal: On his return he went out as State-supporting General and Administrator of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he went out as State-supporting General and Administrator of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 時蕭衍將馬仙琕率眾攻圍朐城，戍主傅文驥嬰城固守。

translations.literal: At that time the Liang general Ma Xianbi led troops to besiege Qucheng; the garrison commander Fu Wenqi held the city with a desperate defense.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Liang general Ma Xianbi besieged Qucheng, whose garrison commander Fu Wenqi held the walls in a desperate defense.

sentences.zh: 以遐持節、假平東將軍為別將，與劉思祖等救之。

translations.literal: Xia, with Bearer of the Staff and acting General Who Pacifies the East, was made a separate commander with Liu Sizu and others to relieve the siege.
translations.idiomatic: xia, with Bearer of the Staff and acting General Who Pacifies the East, was made a separate commander with Liu Sizu and others to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 次於鮑口，去朐城五十里，夏雨頻降，厲涉長驅，將至朐城。

translations.literal: They halted at Baokou, fifty li from Qucheng; summer rains fell in succession, yet they waded through floods and marched at speed, and were about to reach Qucheng.
translations.idiomatic: They halted at Baokou, fifty li from Qucheng; summer rains fell in succession, yet they forced the floods and marched hard, and were about to reach Qucheng.

sentences.zh: 仙琕見遐營壘未就，徑來逆戰。

translations.literal: Xianbi saw that Xia's camp was not yet finished and came straight to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbi saw Xia's camp was not yet set and came straight to give battle.

sentences.zh: 思祖率彭沛之眾，望陳奔退。

translations.literal: Sizu led the Peng and Pei troops and, sighting the enemy array, fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sizu led the Peng and Pei troops and, at sight of the enemy line, broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 遐孤軍奮擊，獨破仙琕，斬其直閤將軍、軍主李魯生，直後軍主葛景羽等。

translations.literal: Xia alone with his army fought fiercely and by himself broke Xianbi, killing his Direct Attendant General and army commander Li Lusheng, Rear Guard army commander Ge Jingyu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Xia alone fought on with his army, broke Xianbi by himself, and killed his Direct Attendant General Li Lusheng, Rear Guard commander Ge Jingyu, and others.

sentences.zh: 仙琕先分軍於朐城之西，阻水列柵，以圍固城。

translations.literal: Xianbi had earlier divided his army west of Qucheng, set palisades across the water, and besieged the fortified city.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbi had earlier divided his army west of Qucheng, thrown palisades across the water, and besieged the fortified city.

sentences.zh: 遐身自潛行，觀水深淺，結草為筏，銜枚夜進，破其六柵，遂解固城之圍。

translations.literal: Xia went in person by secret route to observe the depth of the water, bound reeds into rafts, advanced at night with gags in the soldiers' mouths, broke six palisades, and thus lifted the siege of the fortified city.
translations.idiomatic: Xia went himself by secret paths to test the water, bound reeds into rafts, advanced at night with gags in the men's mouths, broke six palisades, and so lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 進救朐城，都督盧昶率大軍繼之。

translations.literal: He advanced to relieve Qucheng; Overseer Lu Chang led a great army in his wake.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to relieve Qucheng; Overseer Lu Chang followed with a great army.

sentences.zh: 未幾而文驥力竭，以城降賊，眾軍大崩。

translations.literal: Before long Wenqi's strength was spent and he surrendered the city to the enemy; the whole army collapsed in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wenqi's strength failed and he surrendered the city to the enemy; the whole army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 昶棄其節傳，輕騎而走，惟遐獨握節而還。

translations.literal: Chang abandoned his credentials and fled on a light horse; only Xia alone kept his staff and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chang cast off his credentials and fled on a light horse; only Xia kept his staff and returned.

sentences.zh: 時仲冬寒盛，兵士凍死者，朐山至於郯城二百里間僵尸相屬。

translations.literal: It was deep midwinter and bitterly cold; soldiers who froze to death lay corpse beside corpse for two hundred li from Qushan to Tancheng.
translations.idiomatic: It was deep midwinter and bitter cold; men who froze to death lay corpse beside corpse for two hundred li from Qushan to Tancheng.

sentences.zh: 昶儀衞失盡，於郯城借假節以為軍威。

translations.literal: Chang had lost all his guards of honor and borrowed a false staff at Tancheng to restore military prestige.
translations.idiomatic: chang had lost all his guards of honor and borrowed a false staff at Tancheng to restore military prestige.

translations.literal: [1] Xia was demoted for the defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, [1] Xia was demoted for the defeat.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，起為光祿大夫、使持節、假前將軍為別將，防捍西荊，又為別將隸蕭寶夤，東征淮堰。

translations.literal: In the Yanchang reign he was recalled as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Bearer of the Staff, and acting Forward General as a separate commander to defend western Jing; he also served as a separate commander under Xiao Baoyin in the eastern campaign against the Huai embankment.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanchang he was recalled as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Bearer of the Staff, and acting Forward General as a separate commander on the western Jing frontier; he also served as a separate commander under Xiao Baoyin in the eastern campaign against the Huai embankment.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，出為平西將軍、汾州刺史，在州貪濁，聞於遠近。

translations.literal: In the early Xiping reign he went out as General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Fen Province; in the province he was greedy and corrupt, and his name for it spread far and near.
translations.idiomatic: In early Xiping he went out as General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Fen Province, where he was greedy and corrupt and notorious far and wide.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈安南將軍、豫州刺史，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Yu Province, with the posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In his death he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Yu Province, with the posthumous title Xiang.

translations.literal: His son Zixian inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zixian inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 子獻第四弟子素，司空長流參軍。

translations.literal: Zixian's fourth younger brother's son Su was a flowing clerk in the Minister of Works' office.
translations.idiomatic: zixian's fourth younger brother's son Su was a flowing clerk in the Minister of Works' office.

translations.literal: Shulong was Commandant of Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: shulong was Commandant of Foot Soldiers.

sentences.zh: 永平初，同懸瓠城民白早生之逆。

translations.literal: In the early Yongping reign he joined the people of Xuanchi in Bai Zaosheng's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In early Yongping he joined the people of Xuanchi in Bai Zaosheng's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 鎮南邢巒平豫州，獲而宥之。

translations.literal: The Pacify-the-South Commander Xing Luan pacified Yu Province, captured him, and spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Pacify-the-South Commander Xing Luan pacified Yu Province, captured him, and spared him.

translations.literal: Later through bribery he obtained the post of Qin Province
translations.idiomatic: Later, through bribery, he obtained an appointment in Qin Province

translations.idiomatic: He served as appointed Champion General and Palace Counsellor.

translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to General of the Left and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 賂司空劉騰，出為中山內史，在郡無德政，專以貨賄為事。

translations.literal: He bribed the Minister of Works Liu Teng and went out as Interior Minister of Zhongshan; in the commandery he had no virtuous government and dealt solely in bribes.
translations.idiomatic: He bribed Minister of Works Liu Teng and went out as Interior Minister of Zhongshan, where he governed without virtue and dealt solely in bribes.

sentences.zh: 叔隆姦詐無行，忘背恩義。

translations.literal: Shulong was treacherous and deceitful, without conduct, and forgot kindness and betrayed obligation.
translations.idiomatic: Shulong was treacherous and without principle, forgetting kindness and betraying obligation.

sentences.zh: 懸瓠之免，是其族人前軍將軍趙文相之力，後無報德之意，更與文相斷絕，文相長者，不以為恨。

translations.literal: His escape at Xuanchi was due to his clansman Forward General Zhao Wenshang; afterward he showed no gratitude and instead cut ties with Wenshang, who as the elder man did not hold it against him.
translations.idiomatic: His escape at Xuanchi owed to his clansman Forward General Zhao Wenshang; afterward he showed no gratitude and broke with Wenshang, who as the elder bore no resentment.

sentences.zh: 及文相為汝南內史，猶經紀其家。

translations.literal: When Wenshang became Interior Minister of Runan, he still looked after Shulong's household.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wenshang became Interior Minister of Runan, he still looked after Shulong's household.

sentences.zh: 後文相卒，叔隆了不恤其子弟，時論賤薄之。

translations.literal: After Wenshang died, Shulong would not care for his sons and younger brothers; opinion at the time despised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenshang died, Shulong would not care for his sons and younger brothers; public opinion despised him for it.

translations.literal: Mu was skilled at documents and had the knack of the drafting brush.

translations.literal: He was staff officer in the Pacify-the-West headquarters of Fen Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as staff officer in the Pacify-the-West headquarters of Fen Province.

sentences.zh: 翼臨亡，以穆託領軍元叉，以穆為汝南內史。

translations.literal: As Yi lay dying he entrusted Mu to Commander-in-Chief Yuan Cha, and Cha made Mu Interior Minister of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: As Yi lay dying he entrusted Mu to Commander-in-Chief Yuan Cha, who made Mu Interior Minister of Runan.

translations.literal: Hu Fanghui was a man of Linjing in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fanghui came from Linjing in Anding.

translations.literal: His father Yizhou was Yellow Gate Attendant under Yao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yizhou had been Yellow Gate Attendant under Yao Hong.

sentences.zh: 方回，赫連屈丐中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Fanghui was Secretariat Attendant under Helian Qugai.
translations.idiomatic: Fanghui served Helian Qugai as Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 涉獵史籍，辭彩可觀，為屈丐統萬城銘、蛇祠碑諸文，頗行於世。

translations.literal: He ranged through historical records; his literary color was admirable, and he wrote the inscription for Tongwan city, the Snake Shrine stele, and other pieces that circulated widely in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged through historical records and wrote with admirable literary color; his inscription for Tongwan, the Snake Shrine stele, and other pieces circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 世祖破赫連昌，方回入國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu destroyed Helian Chang, Fanghui entered the [Northern Wei] state.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Shizu destroyed Helian Chang, Fanghui entered the [Northern Wei] state.

sentences.zh: 雅有才尚，未為時所知也。

translations.literal: He had refined talent and high aims, yet was not yet known to his age.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, He had refined talent and high aims, yet was not yet known to his age.

sentences.zh: 後為北鎮司馬，為鎮修表，有所稱慶。

translations.literal: Later he was Northern Garrison staff officer; he drafted a memorial for the garrison commander and won praise.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was staff officer of the Northern Garrison; he drafted a memorial for the commander and won praise.

sentences.zh: 世祖覽之，嗟美，問誰所作。

translations.literal: The emperor read it, sighed in admiration, and asked who had written it.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, The emperor read it, sighed in admiration, and asked who had written it.

sentences.zh: 既知方回，召為中書博士，賜爵臨涇子。

translations.literal: Once he knew it was Fanghui, he summoned him and appointed him Secretariat Erudite, enfeoffing him as Viscount of Linjing.
translations.idiomatic: Learning it was Fanghui, he summoned him, appointed him Secretariat Erudite, and enfeoffed him Viscount of Linjing.

sentences.zh: 遷侍郎，與太子少傅游雅等改定律制。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant and, with the Crown Prince Junior Tutor You Ya and others, revised the laws and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant and, with Crown Prince Junior Tutor You Ya and others, revised the laws and regulations.

sentences.zh: 司徒崔浩及當時朝賢，並愛重之。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Cui Hao and the worthies of the court at the time all loved and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Cui Hao and the leading men of the court all loved and esteemed him.

translations.literal: Pure and poor, he kept to the Way and died at a full age.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in purity and poverty, kept to the Way, and died at a full age.

translations.literal: His son Shichang was also a man of mature character and had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shichang was likewise a man of mature character and bore his father's manner.

translations.literal: He rose through posts to Chief Clerk of the Southern Department.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, He rose through posts to Chief Clerk of the Southern Department.

sentences.zh: 子醜孫，中書學生、祕書郎、中散。

translations.literal: His son Chousun was a Secretariat student, Secretariat Gentleman, and Palace Counsellor.
translations.idiomatic: The son Chousun was a Secretariat student, Secretariat Gentleman, and Palace Counsellor.

translations.literal: For generations they did not manage estates; the family was very poor and frugal.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they did not manage estates; the family remained very poor and frugal.

translations.literal: The brothers all died young.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, The brothers all died young.

sentences.zh: 胡叟，字倫許，安定臨涇人也。

translations.literal: Hu Sou, courtesy name Lunxu, was a native of Linjing in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sou, whose courtesy name was Lunxu, came from Linjing in Anding.

translations.literal: His family for generations wore court caps and robes and were a leading clan of Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: His family for generations held court rank and were a leading clan of Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 叟少聰敏，年十三，辨疑釋理，知名鄉國，其意之所悟，與成人交論，尠有屈焉。

translations.literal: Sou was clever and keen from youth; at thirteen he could resolve doubts and explain principle, and was known in his district and state; whatever his mind grasped, when he debated with adults, few could best him.
translations.idiomatic: Sou was clever and keen from youth; at thirteen he could resolve doubts and explain principle and was known throughout his district; in whatever his mind grasped, when he debated with adults, few could best him.

sentences.zh: 學不師受，友人勸之，叟曰：「先聖之言，精義入神者，其唯易乎？

translations.literal: He studied without taking a teacher; when friends urged him, Sou said, "Of the words of the former sages, that whose essential meaning enters the spirit— is it not only the Changes?
translations.idiomatic: He studied without taking a teacher; when friends urged him on, Sou said, "Of the words of the former sages, that whose essential meaning enters the spirit— is it not only the Changes?

translations.literal: One may say that if you think on it, more than half can be mastered.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, One may say that if you think on it, more than half can be mastered.

sentences.zh: 末世腐儒，粗別剛柔之位，寧有探賾未兆者哉。

translations.literal: The rotten Confucians of this degenerate age can barely distinguish the positions of firm and yielding— could there be one who probes the hidden before any sign appears?
translations.idiomatic: The rotten Confucians of this degenerate age can barely distinguish the positions of firm and yielding— could there be one who probes the hidden before any sign appears?.

translations.literal: The pursuit of the Way is not to be found in the present.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, The pursuit of the Way is not to be found in the present.

translations.idiomatic: " When he spread open the mass of writings, a second reading passed before his eyes and all was on his lips.

sentences.zh: 好屬文，既善為典雅之詞，又工為鄙俗之句。

translations.literal: He loved to compose writing; he was skilled both at elegant phrasing and at crafting vulgar lines.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to compose writing, and he was skilled both at elegant phrasing and at crafting vulgar lines.

sentences.zh: 以姚政將衰，遂入長安觀風化，隱匿名行，懼人見知。

translations.literal: Seeing that Yao rule was about to decline, he entered Chang'an to observe its customs, concealing his name as he went, fearing that people would recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Yao rule was about to decline, he entered Chang'an to observe its customs, traveling under a hidden name for fear of being recognized.

sentences.zh: 時京兆韋祖思，少閱典墳，多蔑時輩，知叟至，召而見之。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Zusi of Jingzhao, who had read the classics from youth and held many of his contemporaries in contempt, learned that Sou had arrived and summoned him for a meeting.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Zusi of Jingzhao, who had read the classics from youth and held many contemporaries in contempt, learned Sou had arrived and summoned him.

sentences.zh: 祖思習常，待叟不足，叟聊與敍溫涼，拂衣而出。

translations.literal: Zusi was set in his ways and did not treat Sou adequately; Sou exchanged a few words of greeting and swept his robe and went out.
translations.idiomatic: Zusi was set in his ways and did not treat Sou adequately, and sou exchanged a few words of greeting and swept his robe and went out.

sentences.zh: 祖思固留之，曰：「當與君論天人之際，何遽而反乎？

translations.literal: Zusi pressed him to stay and said, "I ought to discuss heaven and man with you— why turn back so abruptly?
translations.idiomatic: zusi pressed him to stay and said, "I ought to discuss heaven and man with you— why turn back so abruptly?

sentences.zh: 」叟對曰：「論天人者其亡久矣，與君相知，何夸言若是也。

translations.literal: " Sou replied, "Discussion of heaven and man has long been dead; knowing each other as we do, why such boastful talk?
translations.idiomatic: " Sou replied, "Discussion of heaven and man has long been dead, and knowing each other as we do, why such boastful talk?

translations.literal: " He would not sit down and left.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, " He would not sit down and left.

sentences.zh: 至主人家，賦韋杜二族，一宿而成，時年十有八矣。

translations.literal: At his host's house he composed a piece on the Wei and Du clans; in one night it was finished, and he was then eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: In his host's house he composed a piece on the Wei and Du clans; in one night it was finished, and he was then eighteen.

sentences.zh: 其述前載，無違舊美，敍中世有協時事，而末及鄙黷。

translations.literal: In treating earlier records he did not violate old praise; in treating the middle period he matched the times, yet at the end he did not reach vulgar abuse.
translations.idiomatic: In treating earlier records he did not violate old praise, and in treating the middle period he matched the times, yet at the end he did not reach vulgar abuse.

translations.literal: People all marveled at his talent and feared his brush.
translations.idiomatic: people all marveled at his talent and feared his brush.

translations.literal: The age still handed his piece down in recitation, taking it as a jest.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, The age still handed his piece down in recitation, taking it as a jest.

translations.idiomatic: sou, alone and adrift through hardship, had no path to office, and so entered Hanzhong.

translations.literal: Liu Yilong's Liang and Qin Inspector Ji Han of Fengyi, taking Sou for a man of talent, treated him with considerable courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: liu Yilong's Liang and Qin Inspector Ji Han of Fengyi, taking Sou for a man of talent, treated him with considerable courtesy.

translations.literal: He gave Sou a low staff post, which did not suit his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, He gave Sou a low staff post, which did not suit his heart.

sentences.zh: 未幾，翰遷益州，叟隨入蜀，多為豪儁所尚。

translations.literal: Before long Han was transferred to Yizhou and Sou followed him into Shu, where he was much admired by local men of mark.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Han was transferred to Yizhou and Sou followed him into Shu, where he was much admired by local men of mark.

sentences.zh: 時蜀沙門法成，鳩率僧旅，幾于千人，鑄丈六金像。

translations.literal: At that time the Shu monk Facheng gathered the monastic community, nearly a thousand men, and cast a sixteen-foot golden image.
translations.idiomatic: In that time the Shu monk Facheng gathered the monastic community, nearly a thousand men, and cast a sixteen-foot golden image.

sentences.zh: 劉義隆惡其聚眾，將加大辟。

translations.literal: Liu Yilong hated his gathering a crowd and was about to impose the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: liu Yilong hated his gathering a crowd and was about to impose the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 叟聞之，即赴丹陽，啟申其美，遂得免焉。

translations.literal: When Sou heard of it he went at once to Danyang, memorialized the excellence of the act, and Facheng was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sou heard of it he went at once to Danyang, memorialized the excellence of the act, and Facheng was spared.

translations.literal: He returned again to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, He returned again to Shu.

sentences.zh: 法成感之，遺其珍物，價直千餘匹。

translations.literal: Facheng, moved by this, sent him precious goods worth more than a thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: facheng, moved by this, sent him precious goods worth more than a thousand bolts.

sentences.zh: 叟謂法成曰：「緯蕭何人，能棄明珠？

translations.literal: Sou said to Facheng, "What sort of man was Wei Xiao that he could cast aside bright pearls?
translations.idiomatic: sou said to Facheng, "What sort of man was Wei Xiao that he could cast aside bright pearls?

translations.literal: I pleaded on grounds of virtue— what is wealth to me?
translations.idiomatic: I pleaded on grounds of virtue— what is wealth to me?.

translations.literal: " He accepted not a single thing.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, " He accepted not a single thing.

translations.literal: In the Yi region five or six years, he went north to Yang Dang, then west to Juqu Mujian, who did not esteem him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yi region five or six years, he went north to Yang Dang, then west to Juqu Mujian, who did not esteem him.

sentences.zh: 叟亦本無附之之誠，乃為詩示所知廣平程伯達。

translations.literal: Sou likewise had no intention of attaching himself; he composed a poem to show his acquaintance Cheng Boda of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Sou likewise had no intention of attaching himself, and he composed a poem to show his acquaintance Cheng Boda of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：「羣犬吠新客，佞闇排疏賓。

translations.literal: In outline it said, "The pack of dogs bark at the new guest; the flatterers in darkness drive off the plain guest.
translations.idiomatic: In outline it said, "The pack of dogs bark at the new guest, and the flatterers in darkness drive off the plain guest.

sentences.zh: 直途既以塞，曲路非所遵。

translations.literal: The straight road is already blocked; the crooked path is not what I follow.
translations.idiomatic: The straight road is already blocked, and the crooked path is not what I follow.

sentences.zh: 望衞惋祝鮀，眄楚悼靈均。

translations.literal: Gazing toward Wei I pity Zhu Tuo; looking toward Chu I mourn Qu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing toward Wei I pity Zhu Tuo, and looking toward Chu I mourn Qu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 何用宣憂懷，託翰寄輔仁。

translations.literal: Why use words to declare sorrow? I entrust my brush to Fu Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, Why use words to declare sorrow? I entrust my brush to Fu Ren.

sentences.zh: 」伯達見詩，謂叟曰：「涼州雖地居戎域，然自張氏以來，號有華風。

translations.literal: " When Boda saw the poem he said to Sou, "Liang Province, though it lies in the barbarian domain, yet from the Zhang clan onward has been called to have a Chinese air.
translations.idiomatic: " When Boda saw the poem he said to Sou, "Liang Province, though it lies in the barbarian domain, yet from the Zhang clan onward has been called to have a Chinese air.

translations.literal: Now its laws and standards are unimpaired— how can there be a Zhu Tuo?
translations.idiomatic: Now its laws and standards are unimpaired— how can there be a Zhu Tuo?.

translations.literal: " Sou said, "The ancients had a saying: when a gentleman hears the sound of drums and flails, he thinks of the men of war.
translations.idiomatic: " Sou said, "The ancients had a saying: when a gentleman hears the sound of drums and flails, he thinks of the men of war.

sentences.zh: 貴主奉正朔而弗淳，慕仁義而未允，地陋僻而僭徽號。

translations.literal: Your honored lord receives the royal calendar yet is not pure, admires benevolence and righteousness yet is not sincere, the land is narrow and remote yet he usurps imperial emblems.
translations.idiomatic: your honored lord receives the royal calendar yet is not pure, admires benevolence and righteousness yet is not sincere, the land is narrow and remote yet he usurps imperial emblems.

translations.literal: To dwell in smallness yet act as if great— can it be like this?
translations.idiomatic: To dwell in smallness yet act as if great— can it be like this?.

translations.literal: The wheel-tracks of Xu Yan will not turn back in a hurry.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, The wheel-tracks of Xu Yan will not turn back in a hurry.

sentences.zh: 吾之擇木，夙在大魏，與子暫違，非久闊也。

translations.literal: My choice of a tree has long been in Great Wei; with you I part for a time— it is not a long separation.
translations.idiomatic: My choice of a tree has long been in Great Wei, and with you I part for a time— it is not a long separation.

translations.literal: " After a year and more, Mujian was destroyed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, " After a year and more, Mujian was destroyed and submitted.

sentences.zh: 叟既先歸國，朝廷以其識機，拜虎威將軍，賜爵始復男。

translations.literal: Sou had already returned to the state first; the court, because he had read the signs, appointed him General of Tiger Might and enfeoffed him as Baron of Shifu.
translations.idiomatic: Sou had already returned to the state first; the court, because he had read the signs, appointed him General of Tiger Might and enfeoffed him Baron of Shifu.

sentences.zh: 家於密雲，蓬室草筵，惟以酒自適。

translations.literal: He made his home in Miyun in a thatched hut with a grass mat, finding his ease only in wine.
translations.idiomatic: He made his home in Miyun in a thatched hut with a grass mat, finding his ease only in wine.

sentences.zh: 謂友人金城宗舒曰：「我此生活，似勝焦先，志意所栖，謝其高矣。

translations.literal: He said to his friend Zong Shu of Jincheng, "This life of mine seems better than Jiao Xian's; the place my will inhabits— I yield the height to him.
translations.idiomatic: He said to his friend Zong Shu of Jincheng, "This life of mine seems better than Jiao Xian's, and the place my will inhabits— I yield the height to him.

sentences.zh: 」後叟被徵至，謝恩，并獻詩一篇。

translations.literal: " Later when Sou was summoned to court to give thanks, he also presented a poem.
translations.idiomatic: " Later when Sou was summoned to court to give thanks, he also presented a poem.

sentences.zh: 高宗時召叟及舒，並使作檄劉駿、蠕蠕文。

translations.literal: In Emperor Gaozong's time Sou and Shu were both summoned and ordered to draft proclamations against Liu Jun and the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Gaozong's time Sou and Shu were both summoned and ordered to draft proclamations against Liu Jun and the Rouran.

translations.literal: Shu's text was inferior to Sou's; Shu soon returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's text was inferior to Sou's, and shu soon returned home.

sentences.zh: 叟不治產業，常苦飢貧，然不以為耻。

translations.literal: Sou did not manage estates and was often bitterly hungry and poor, yet he did not take it as shame.
translations.idiomatic: sou did not manage estates and was often bitterly hungry and poor, yet he did not take it as shame.

translations.literal: He adopted a son styled Mingling to support and sustain himself.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, He adopted a son styled Mingling to support and sustain himself.

sentences.zh: 每至貴勝之門，恒乘一牸牛，弊韋袴褶而已。

translations.literal: Whenever he came to the gates of the noble and eminent he always rode a single cow, wearing only worn leather trousers and jacket.
translations.idiomatic: whenever he came to the gates of the noble and eminent he always rode a single cow, wearing only worn leather trousers and jacket.

sentences.zh: 作布囊，容三四斗，飲噉醉飽，便盛餘肉餅以付螟蛉。

translations.literal: He made a cloth sack holding three or four dou; when he had drunk and eaten his fill in drunkenness, he would pack the leftover meat and cakes for Mingling.
translations.idiomatic: He made a cloth sack holding three or four dou; when he had drunk and eaten his fill, he would pack the leftover meat and cakes for Mingling.

sentences.zh: 見車馬榮華者，視之蔑如也。

translations.literal: When he saw carriages, horses, glory, and splendor he regarded them with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Once he saw carriages, horses, glory, and splendor he regarded them with contempt.

sentences.zh: 尚書李敷，嘗遺之以財，都無所取。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Li Fu once sent him wealth; he took none of it at all.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Li Fu once sent him wealth, and he took none of it at all.

sentences.zh: 初叟一見高允，曰：「吳鄭之交，以紵縞為美談，吾之於子，以弦韋為幽贄，以此言之，彼可無愧也。

translations.literal: When Sou first met Gao Yun he said, "The friendship of Wu and Zheng, with coarse silk as its fine talk— between you and me, with bowstring and leather as a humble gift, in this I need not be ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sou first met Gao Yun he said, "The friendship of Wu and Zheng, with coarse silk as its fine talk— between you and me, with bowstring and leather as a humble gift, in this I need not be ashamed.

translations.literal: " At Yun's lodge he met Secretariat Attendant Li Can of Zhao commandery; Can was dressed in splendid finery while Sou was an old man in poor brown clothes, and Can slighted him somewhat.

translations.idiomatic: Both ends can be kept— where are Hui and Ci?

translations.idiomatic: When Cui Hao was executed, Qin was condemned to death as well.

sentences.zh: 欽在河西，撰蒙遜記十卷，無足可稱。

translations.literal: While Qin was in Hexi he compiled a Record of Mengxun in ten juan, not worth mention.
translations.idiomatic: While in Hexi he compiled a ten-juan Record of Mengxun, not worth mention.

translations.literal: His younger brother Shu, courtesy name Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shu, whose courtesy name was Jingtai.

translations.literal: Director of the Treasury under Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: He was Director of the Treasury under Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 與兄同歸國，賜爵句町男，加威遠將軍。

translations.literal: He returned to the state with his elder brother and was enfeoffed Baron of Gouding, with the additional title General of Awesome Might.
translations.idiomatic: He returned with his elder brother and was enfeoffed Baron of Gouding, with the additional title General of Awesome Might.

translations.literal: His fame was second to his elder brother's.
translations.idiomatic: His fame stood second to his elder brother's.

translations.literal: Descendants all declined in standing.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants all declined in standing.

sentences.zh: 段承根，武威姑臧人，自云漢太尉熲九世孫也。

translations.literal: Duan Chenggen was a man of Guzang in Wuwei and said himself to be ninth-generation descendant of Han Grand Commandant Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Chenggen came from Guzang in Wuwei and claimed descent from Han Grand Commandant Ying, nine generations removed.

sentences.zh: 父暉，字長祚，身長八尺餘，師事歐陽湯，湯甚器愛之。

translations.literal: His father Hui, courtesy name Changzuo, was more than eight feet in height; he took Ouyang Tang as teacher and Tang greatly prized him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui, whose courtesy name was Changzuo, stood more than eight feet tall; he studied under Ouyang Tang, who greatly prized him.

translations.literal: There was a youth who shared Hui's aims.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, There was a youth who shared Hui's aims.

sentences.zh: 後二年，童子辭歸，從暉請馬。

translations.literal: Two years later the youth took leave to return and asked Hui for a horse.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, Two years later the youth took leave to return and asked Hui for a horse.

translations.literal: Hui in jest made him a wooden horse.
translations.idiomatic: hui in jest made him a wooden horse.

sentences.zh: 童子甚悅，謝暉曰：「吾太山府君子，奉敕遊學，今將欲歸。

translations.literal: The youth was very pleased and thanked Hui: "I am a gentleman of the Taishan prefecture, sent on tour to study by command; now I am about to return.
translations.idiomatic: The youth was delighted and thanked Hui: "I am a gentleman of the Taishan prefecture, sent to study by command; now I must return.

translations.literal: I trouble you for a generous gift and have no virtue with which to repay.
translations.idiomatic: I trouble you for a generous gift and have no virtue with which to repay it.

translations.literal: You later will reach Regular Attendant and be enfeoffed marquis.
translations.idiomatic: You will later reach Regular Attendant and be enfeoffed marquis.

translations.literal: It is not repayment— it is only to seal friendship.
translations.idiomatic: It is not repayment— only to seal our friendship.

translations.literal: " When he finished speaking he mounted the wooden horse and soared into the air and left.
translations.idiomatic: " When he finished he mounted the wooden horse and soared into the air.

translations.literal: Hui then knew he himself was destined for eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then knew he was destined for eminence.

sentences.zh: 乞伏熾磐以暉為輔國大將軍、涼州刺史、御史大夫、西海侯。

translations.literal: Fu Qini's Chiqian made Hui State-supporting Grand General, Governor of Liang Province, Imperial Secretary, and Marquis of Xihai.
translations.idiomatic: Chiqian of the Fu clan made Hui State-supporting Grand General, Governor of Liang Province, Imperial Secretary, and Marquis of Xihai.

sentences.zh: 磐子暮末襲位，國政衰亂，暉父子奔吐谷渾暮璝，暮璝內附，暉與承根歸國。

translations.literal: When Chiqian's son Mumo succeeded, state affairs decayed and were chaotic; Hui and his son fled to Murong Mujun of the Tuyuhun; when Mujun submitted inward, Hui and Chenggen returned to the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Chiqian's son Mumo succeeded, the state decayed; Hui and his son fled to Murong Mujun of the Tuyuhun, and when Mujun submitted inward, Hui and Chenggen returned.

sentences.zh: 世祖素聞其名，頗重之，以為上客。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu had long heard his name and greatly valued him, making him a senior guest.
translations.idiomatic: emperor Shizu had long heard his name and greatly valued him, making him a senior guest.

sentences.zh: 後暉從世祖至長安，有人告暉欲南奔，世祖問曰：「何以知之？

translations.literal: Later when Hui followed the emperor to Chang'an, someone reported that Hui intended to flee south. The emperor asked, "How do you know?"
translations.idiomatic: Later when Hui followed the emperor to Chang'an, someone reported he intended to flee south. The emperor asked, "How do you know?"

sentences.zh: 」告者曰：「暉置金於馬韉中，不欲逃走，何由爾也？

translations.literal: " The informant said, "Hui placed gold in his saddlebags— if he did not wish to flee, why else?"
translations.idiomatic: " The informant said, "Hui placed gold in his saddlebags— if he did not wish to flee, why else?"

sentences.zh: 」世祖密遣視之，果如告者之言，斬之於市，曝尸數日。

translations.literal: " The emperor secretly sent men to look and it was exactly as the informant said; Hui was beheaded in the market and his corpse exposed several days.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent men to look and it was as reported; Hui was beheaded in the market and his corpse exposed several days.

sentences.zh: 時有儒生京兆林白奴欽暉德音，夜竊其尸，置之枯井。

translations.literal: At that time the Confucian Lin Bainu of Jingzhao admired Hui's virtuous tone; at night he stole the corpse and placed it in a dry well.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Confucian Lin Bainu of Jingzhao admired Hui's virtue; at night he stole the corpse and placed it in a dry well.

sentences.zh: 女為敦煌張氏婦，久而聞之，乃向長安收葬。

translations.literal: His daughter was wife to a man of the Zhang clan of Dunhuang; long afterward she heard of it and went to Chang'an to collect and bury him.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter had married into the Zhang clan of Dunhuang; long afterward she heard and went to Chang'an to collect and bury him.

sentences.zh: 承根好學、機辯，有文思，而性行疏薄，有始無終。

translations.literal: Chenggen loved learning and was clever in debate, with literary thought, yet by nature loose and thin, with beginnings but no ends.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggen loved learning and was clever in debate, with literary gifts, yet by nature loose and unreliable, starting things he did not finish.

sentences.zh: 司徒崔浩見而奇之，以為才堪注述，言之世祖，請為著作郎，引與同事。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Cui Hao saw him and marveled, thinking his talent fit commentary and writing; he spoke of him to Emperor Shizu, who requested him as Drafting Secretary and drew him into collaboration.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao saw him and marveled, thinking his talent fit commentary; he spoke to Emperor Shizu, who made him Drafting Secretary and drew him into collaboration.

translations.literal: The age all valued his writing but despised his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The age valued his writing but despised his conduct.

sentences.zh: 甚為敦煌公李寶所敬待，承根贈寶詩曰：「世道衰陵，淳風殆緬。

translations.literal: He was greatly respected and entertained by Prince Li of Dunhuang; Chenggen presented Bao with a poem saying, "The age's way declines and falls; pure wind nearly perishes.
translations.idiomatic: He was greatly respected by Prince Li of Dunhuang; Chenggen presented Bao with a poem: "The age declines; pure wind nearly perishes.

translations.literal: Crossroads contend for the tripod; the road is full of those seeking gems.
translations.idiomatic: At the crossroads they contend for the tripod; the road is full of gem-seekers.

translations.literal: Racing in pursuit they gallop; heaven's mechanism none treads.
translations.idiomatic: Racing in pursuit they gallop, and heaven's mechanism none treads.

translations.literal: Without the true ruler, who will clear the brambles?
translations.idiomatic: Without the true ruler, who will clear the brambles?.

translations.idiomatic: 〈one〉

translations.literal: How glorious our empress, doubled radiance heaped bright.
translations.idiomatic: How glorious our empress— doubled radiance heaped bright.

translations.literal: Pattern to quiet vexation; martial to still disorder.
translations.idiomatic: By pattern to quiet vexation; by martial arts to still disorder.

translations.literal: Split the clam to seek the pearl; search the cliffs to gather dry wood.
translations.idiomatic: Split the clam to seek the pearl; search the cliffs for dry timber.

translations.literal: In the wild none cast the line; at court overflowed retiring brush.
translations.idiomatic: In the wild none cast the line; at court retiring brush overflowed.

translations.literal: 〈two〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈two〉

translations.literal: From the Liang season of old, forests burned and pools dried.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, From the Liang season of old, forests burned and pools dried.

translations.literal: Lofty, lofty the young lord— scales and feathers had nowhere to lodge.
translations.idiomatic: lofty, lofty the young lord— scales and feathers had nowhere to lodge.

translations.literal: Spirit wisdom though it stirred, demonic vapors were not cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, Spirit wisdom though it stirred, demonic vapors were not cleared.

translations.literal: The phoenix folded at Kunqiu; the dragon hid in dark vastness.
translations.idiomatic: The phoenix folded at Kunqiu, and the dragon hid in dark vastness.

translations.literal: 〈three〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈three〉

translations.literal: Numbers do not always disturb; when hardship reaches the limit then ease.
translations.idiomatic: Numbers do not always disturb; at extremity of hardship comes ease.

translations.literal: He flaps wings in the dark frontier; brush flying to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He flaps wings in the dark frontier; brush flies to the capital.

translations.literal: Earring cicada at the purple gate; staff and tally in the square domain.
translations.idiomatic: Earring cicada at the purple gate, and staff and tally in the square domain.

translations.literal: He assists our king's measure; the many achievements are gathered bright.
translations.idiomatic: He assists our king's measure; many achievements gather bright.

translations.literal: 〈four〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈four〉

translations.literal: Since I was sunk in the dark, I cherished old bond.
translations.idiomatic: Since I was sunk in the dark, I cherished our old bond.

translations.literal: May I shelter in your remaining light and pass the year at ease.
translations.idiomatic: may I shelter in your remaining light and pass the year at ease.

translations.literal: The glad road not yet flooded; the parting reins already at the border.
translations.idiomatic: The glad road not yet flooded; parting reins already at the border.

translations.literal: Looking back at hard division— now stretched, now gathered.
translations.idiomatic: looking back at hard division— now stretched, now gathered.

translations.literal: 〈five〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈five〉

translations.literal: I hear from friends of old, sage piled on sage.
translations.idiomatic: I hear from friends of old— sage piled on sage.

translations.literal: Though the pure source is thin, the people keep its remaining strength.
translations.idiomatic: Though the pure source runs thin, the people keep its remaining strength.

translations.literal: I think with joy on the wise man; stillness quells rashness.
translations.idiomatic: I think with joy on the wise man, and stillness quells rashness.

translations.literal: Lush is that complex tone; harmonize with this clear tune.
translations.idiomatic: Lush is that complex tone— harmonize with this clear tune.

translations.literal: 〈six〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈six〉

translations.literal: Inquiring below is called pattern; distinguishing accusations is called clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiring below is called pattern, and distinguishing accusations is called clarity.

translations.literal: Transformation through ritual harmony; government through leniency succeeds.
translations.idiomatic: Transformation through ritual harmony, and government through leniency succeeds.

translations.literal: Exhort to honor benevolent teaching; spread virtue and simplify punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Exhort to honor benevolent teaching, and spread virtue and simplify punishment.

translations.idiomatic: I bow my head to the fair wind, slow to hear the restful sound.".
