translations.idiomatic: 〈seven〉

sentences.zh: 浩誅，承根與宗欽等俱死。

translations.literal: When Hao was executed, Chenggen died with Zong Qin and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was executed, Chenggen died together with Zong Qin and others.

sentences.zh: 承根外孫長水校尉南陽張令言，美鬚髯，言談舉止，有異武人。

translations.literal: Chenggen's daughter's son Zhang Lingyan, Commandant of Everflowing Waters, of Nanyang— beautiful beard and mustache, speech and conduct unlike a military man.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson by a daughter, Zhang Lingyan, Commandant of Everflowing Waters of Nanyang— fine beard and mustache, speech and conduct unlike a soldier.

sentences.zh: 李琰之、李神儁，一時名士，並稱美之。

translations.literal: Li Yanzhi and Li Shenjun, famous men of the time, both praised him.
translations.idiomatic: li Yanzhi and Li Shenjun, famous men of the time, both praised him.

translations.literal: Yan Yin, courtesy name Xuanyin, was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yin, whose courtesy name was Xuanyin, came from Dunhuang.

translations.literal: His grandfather Liang was famed in the western lands.
translations.idiomatic: The grandfather Liang was famed in the western lands.

sentences.zh: 父玟，為一時秀士，官至會稽令。

translations.literal: His father Min was a talent of the age and reached the post of Magistrate of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: His father Min was a talent of the age and reached Magistrate of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 駰博通經傳，聰敏過人，三史羣言，經目則誦，時人謂之宿讀。

translations.literal: Yin ranged broadly through the classics and transmissions, clever beyond others; the Three Histories and all schools— once he glanced he could recite; men of the time called him one who had read overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Yin mastered the classics and transmissions, clever beyond others; the Three Histories and all schools— at a glance he could recite; men called him an overnight reader.

sentences.zh: 注王朗易傳，學者藉以通經。

translations.literal: He annotated Wang Lang's commentary on the Changes, and scholars relied on it to penetrate the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated Wang Lang's commentary on the Changes, and scholars relied on it to master the classics.

translations.literal: He compiled the Gazetteer of the Thirteen Provinces, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled the Gazetteer of the Thirteen Provinces, which circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜甚重之，常侍左右，訪以政治損益。

translations.literal: Mengxun greatly valued him and kept him always at his side, consulting on the gains and losses of government.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun greatly valued him, kept him at his side, and consulted on government gains and losses.

sentences.zh: 拜祕書考課郎中，給文吏三十人，典校經籍，刊定諸子三千餘卷。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretariat Examination Gentleman, given thirty clerical officials, charged with collating the classics and editing more than three thousand juan of the various masters.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Secretariat Examination Gentleman, given thirty clerical officials, and charged with collating the classics and editing more than three thousand juan of the masters.

translations.literal: He was given the additional title Commandant of the Imperial Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He served as given the additional title Commandant of the Imperial Carriage.

sentences.zh: 牧犍待之彌重，拜大行，遷尚書。

translations.literal: Mujian treated him still more heavily, appointing him Grand Messenger and promoting him to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: mujian treated him still more heavily, appointing him Grand Messenger and promoting him to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 姑臧平，樂平王丕鎮涼州，引為從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Guzang was pacified, Prince Ping of Le'an pacified Liang Province and drew Yin as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guzang was pacified, Prince Ping of Le'an pacified Liang Province and drew Yin as staff officer.

translations.literal: After the prince died he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, After the prince died he returned to the capital.

translations.literal: His family was very poor and shabby; he could not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: His family was very poor; he could not escape hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 性能多食，一飯至三升乃飽。

translations.literal: By nature he could eat much; one meal to three sheng before he was full.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he ate heavily; one meal took three sheng before he was full.

translations.literal: At his death he had no posterity.
translations.idiomatic: He died without posterity.

translations.literal: Liu Bing, courtesy name Yanming, was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bing, whose courtesy name was Yanming, came from Dunhuang.

translations.literal: His father Bao, courtesy name Ziyu, was famed for Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bao, whose courtesy name was Ziyu, was famed for Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 昞年十四，就博士郭瑀學。

translations.literal: At fourteen Bing went to study with Erudite Guo Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In fourteen Bing went to study with Erudite Guo Yu.

sentences.zh: 時瑀弟子五百餘人，通經業者八十餘人。

translations.literal: At that time Yu had more than five hundred disciples; those who had mastered the classics numbered more than eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had more than five hundred disciples; more than eighty had mastered the classics.

sentences.zh: 瑀有女始笄，妙選良偶，有心於昞。

translations.literal: Yu had a daughter just at her hair-pinning; he finely chose a good match and had his heart set on Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had a daughter just come of age; he sought a fine son-in-law and favored Bing.

sentences.zh: 遂別設一席於坐前，謂諸弟子曰：「吾有一女，年向成長，欲覓一快女壻，誰坐此席者，吾當婚焉。

translations.literal: He then set out a separate seat before the assembly and said to the disciples, "I have a daughter nearly grown; I wish to find a fine son-in-law— whoever sits in this seat I will marry her to."
translations.idiomatic: He set a separate seat before the assembly and said, "I have a daughter nearly grown and seek a fine son-in-law— whoever sits here shall marry her."

sentences.zh: 」昞遂奮衣來坐，神志肅然，曰：「向聞先生欲求快女壻，昞其人也。

translations.literal: Bing then swept his robe and came to sit, spirit and bearing solemn, and said, "I have heard the master seeks a fine son-in-law— Bing is the man."
translations.idiomatic: Bing swept his robe, sat down with solemn bearing, and said, "I hear you seek a fine son-in-law— I am the man."

translations.literal: Yu then gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: yu then gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 昞後隱居酒泉，不應州郡之命，弟子受業者五百餘人。

translations.literal: Later Bing lived in seclusion at Jiuquan and did not respond to provincial and commandery orders; disciples who received his teaching numbered more than five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Later Bing lived in seclusion at Jiuquan, ignored provincial orders, and taught more than five hundred disciples.

sentences.zh: 李暠私署，徵為儒林祭酒、從事中郎。

translations.literal: Li Gao privately appointed him Libationer of the Forest of Scholars and Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: li Gao privately appointed him Libationer of the Forest of Scholars and Attendant.

sentences.zh: 暠好尚文典，書史穿落者親自補治，昞時侍側，前請代暠。

translations.literal: Gao loved literary canons; when books and histories were worn and falling apart he personally repaired them, and Bing at times attended at his side and stepped forward offering to replace Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Gao loved the literary canon; when books were worn he repaired them himself, and Bing would offer to do it for him.

sentences.zh: 暠曰：「躬自執者，欲人重此典籍。

translations.literal: Gao said, "When I handle it myself I want men to value these classics.
translations.idiomatic: gao said, "When I handle it myself I want men to value these classics.

sentences.zh: 吾與卿相值，何異孔明之會玄德。

translations.literal: You and I have met— how is it different from Kongming meeting Xuande?"
translations.idiomatic: You and I have met— how is it different from Kongming meeting Xuande?".

sentences.zh: 」遷撫夷護軍，雖有政務，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: He was transferred Pacify-the-Barbarians Protector of the Army; though he had government affairs he never laid book from hand.
translations.idiomatic: He became Pacify-the-Barbarians Protector of the Army; though he held office he never laid book from hand.

sentences.zh: 暠曰：「卿注記篇籍，以燭繼晝。

translations.literal: Gao said, "You annotate and record texts, using candles to continue daylight.
translations.idiomatic: Gao said, "You annotate texts by candle into daylight.

translations.literal: Even in daytime it is so— at night you should rest."
translations.idiomatic: Even by day it is so— at night you should rest."

sentences.zh: 」昞曰：「朝聞道，夕死可矣，不知老之將至，孔聖稱焉。

translations.literal: Bing said, "If one hears the Way in the morning, one may die in the evening— not knowing old age approaches, Confucius praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Bing said, "Hear the Way in the morning and one may die at evening— not knowing old age nears, as Confucius praised.

translations.literal: What sort of man is Bing that he dares not be like this?"
translations.idiomatic: What sort of man is Bing that he dares not do likewise?"

sentences.zh: 」昞以三史文繁，著略記百三十篇、八十四卷，涼書十卷，敦煌實錄二十卷，方言三卷，靖恭堂銘一卷，注周易、韓子、人物志、黃石公三略，並行於世。

translations.literal: Bing, because the Three Histories were cumbersome in text, composed Outline Records in 130 pieces and 84 juan, Liang History in 10 juan, Veritable Records of Dunhuang in 20 juan, Dialect in 3 juan, Inscription for the Jinggong Hall in 1 juan, and commentaries on the Changes, Han Feizi, Records of Men, and the Yellow Stone Lord's Three Strategies— all circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Three Histories were cumbersome, Bing composed Outline Records in 130 pieces and 84 juan, Liang History, Dunhuang Veritable Records, Dialect, the Jinggong Hall inscription, and commentaries on the Changes, Han Feizi, Records of Men, and the Three Strategies— all circulating in the world.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜平酒泉，拜祕書郎，專管注記。

translations.literal: When Mengxun pacified Jiuquan, Bing was appointed Secretariat Gentleman in charge of annotation.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mengxun pacified Jiuquan, Bing was appointed Secretariat Gentleman in charge of annotation.

sentences.zh: 築陸沉觀於西苑，躬往禮焉，號「玄處先生」，學徒數百，月致羊酒。

translations.literal: He built the Sunken-in-the-Land Observatory in the western park; Mengxun went in person to pay ritual respect and styled him "Master of the Hidden Abode"; disciples numbered in the hundreds and each month presented sheep and wine.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Sunken-in-the-Land Observatory in the western park; Mengxun paid ritual respect in person and styled him Master of the Hidden Abode; hundreds of disciples presented sheep and wine monthly.

sentences.zh: 牧犍尊為國師，親自致拜，命官屬以下皆北面受業焉。

translations.literal: Mujian honored him as National Teacher, bowed in person, and ordered officials and subordinates all to face north and receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Mujian honored him as National Teacher, bowed in person, and ordered all officials to face north and receive instruction.

sentences.zh: 時同郡索敞、陰興為助教，並以文學見舉，每巾衣而入。

translations.literal: At that time Suo Chang and Yin Xing of the same commandery were assistant teachers; both were recommended for literary learning and each entered in scholar's dress.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chang and Yin Xing of the same commandery were assistant teachers, recommended for literary learning, each entering in scholar's dress.

sentences.zh: 世祖平涼州，士民東遷，夙聞其名，拜樂平王從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu pacified Liang Province the gentry and people moved east; he had long heard Bing's name and appointed him staff officer to Prince Ping of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu pacified Liang Province, he had long heard Bing's name and appointed him staff officer to Prince Ping of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔諸年七十以上聽留本鄉，一子扶養。

translations.literal: The emperor decreed that those over seventy might remain in their native districts with one son to support them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decreed that those over seventy might remain in their native districts with one son to support them.

sentences.zh: 昞時老矣，在姑臧，歲餘，思鄉而返，至涼州西四百里韭谷窟，[5]遇疾而卒。

translations.literal: Bing was then old and in Guzang; after a year and more he longed for home and returned; at Jiugu Cave four hundred li west of Liang Province [5] he met illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: Bing was then old in Guzang; after a year he longed for home and returned; at Jiugu Cave west of Liang Province [5] he fell ill and died.

translations.literal: Bing had six sons.
translations.idiomatic: bing had six sons.

translations.literal: His eldest son Sengyan died young.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Sengyan died young.

translations.literal: The second, Zhongli, remained in the native district.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, The second, Zhongli, remained in the native district.

sentences.zh: 次字仲，次貳歸，少歸仁，並遷代京。

translations.literal: The third Zi, the fourth Ergui, and the fifth Shaoguiren all moved to the capital of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The third Zi, fourth Ergui, and fifth Shaoguiren all moved to the capital of Dai.

translations.literal: Later they were assigned to various provinces as garrison commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, they were assigned to various provinces as garrison commoners.

sentences.zh: 歸仁有二子，長買奴，次顯宗。

translations.literal: Shaoguiren had two sons, the elder Mainu and the younger Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoguiren had two sons, Mainu and Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 太和十四年，尚書李沖奏，昞河右碩儒，今子孫沉屈，未有祿潤，賢者子孫宜蒙顯異。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Taihe, Secretariat Director Li Chong memorialized that Bing was a great scholar of the He-you region and his descendants were sunk low without stipend— worthy men's descendants ought to receive special favor.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 14 Secretariat Director Li Chong memorialized that Bing was a great He-you scholar whose descendants languished without stipend— worthy descendants ought to receive favor.

sentences.zh: 於是除其一子為郢州雲陽令。

translations.literal: Thereupon one of his sons was made Magistrate of Yunyang in Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon one son was made Magistrate of Yunyang in Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 正光三年，太保崔光奏曰：「臣聞太上立德，其次立功、立言。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengguang Grand Guardian Cui Guang memorialized: "I have heard that the highest establishes virtue, next merit, next words.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengguang 3 Grand Guardian Cui Guang memorialized: "I hear the highest establishes virtue, next merit, next words.

translations.literal: Not dying yet remaining— the former sages honored this;
translations.idiomatic: To die yet not perish— the sages honored this;

translations.literal: thinking of a man, loving his tree— from old it was called beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: thinking of a man, loving his tree— from old called beautiful.

sentences.zh: 故樂平王從事中郎敦煌劉昞，著業涼城，遺文茲在，篇籍之美，頗足可觀。

translations.literal: Therefore Liu Bing, Attendant to Prince Ping of Le'an of Dunhuang, established his work in Liang city; his surviving writings are here; the beauty of his texts is quite worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bing, staff officer to Prince Ping of Le'an, established his work in Liang; his writings remain and are worth viewing.

sentences.zh: 如或愆釁，當蒙數世之宥，況乃維祖逮孫，相去未遠，而令久淪皂隸，不獲收異，儒學之士，所為竊歎。

translations.literal: If there was fault it should receive pardon through generations; how much more when forebears reach descendants across no great distance— yet they long sink among the black-clad and receive no special treatment; men of Confucian learning sigh in secret for this.
translations.idiomatic: Fault might win pardon for generations; how much more when forebears and descendants are near— yet they sink among the black-clad; Confucians sigh for this.

sentences.zh: 臣忝職史教，[6]冒以聞奏，乞敕尚書，推檢所屬，甄免碎役，用廣聖朝旌善繼絕。

translations.literal: Your servant, shamed in the post of history instruction [6], ventures this memorial, begging the Secretariat to examine their jurisdictions, select and exempt petty service, to broaden the court's honoring of good and continuing the cut off.
translations.idiomatic: I venture this memorial, begging the Secretariat examine and exempt petty service, to broaden honoring good and continuing the cut off.

translations.literal: Uplifting transformation and stern custom lie in this."
translations.idiomatic: uplifting transformation and stern custom lie in this."

sentences.zh: 」四年六月詔曰：「昞德冠前世，蔚為儒宗，太保啟陳，深合勸善。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year an edict said: "Bing's virtue topped former ages; he was luxuriant as patriarch of Confucians; the Grand Guardian's memorial deeply fits encouraging good.
translations.idiomatic: In month 6 of year 4 an edict said: "Bing's virtue topped former ages; he was patriarch of Confucians; the Grand Guardian's memorial fits encouraging good.

translations.literal: His grandsons and the three families are specially permitted exemption."
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons and three families are specially exempted."

translations.literal: The people of Hexi took it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, The people of Hexi took it as glory.

translations.literal: Zhao Rou, courtesy name Yuanshun, was a man of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Rou, whose courtesy name was Yuanshun, came from Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 少以德行才學知名河右。

translations.literal: From youth he was known west of the Yellow River for virtue, conduct, talent, and learning.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was known west of the Yellow River for virtue, conduct, talent, and learning.

translations.literal: In Juqu Mujian's time he was Director of the Gold Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Under Juqu Mujian he was Director of the Gold Bureau.

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu pacified Liang Province he was moved inward to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu pacified Liang Province he was moved to the capital.

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended he was appointed Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Gaozong ascended he was appointed Drafting Secretary.

sentences.zh: 後以歷効有績，出為河內太守，甚著仁惠。

translations.literal: Later for accumulated merit he went out as Administrator of Henei and was very noted for benevolence and grace.
translations.idiomatic: Later for accumulated merit he went out as Administrator of Henei, very noted for benevolence.

sentences.zh: 柔嘗在路得人所遺金珠一貫，價直數百縑，柔呼主還之。

translations.literal: Rou once on the road found a string of gold pearls another had lost, worth several hundred bolts of silk; Rou called the owner to return them.
translations.idiomatic: Rou once found a lost string of gold pearls worth hundreds of bolts of silk and called the owner to return them.

sentences.zh: 後有人與柔鏵數百枚者，柔與子善明鬻之於市。

translations.literal: Later someone gave Rou several hundred plowshares; Rou and his son Shanming sold them in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone gave Rou several hundred plowshares; he and his son Shanming sold them in the market.

translations.literal: Someone bought from Rou and asked for twenty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: A buyer asked for twenty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 有商人知其賤，與柔三十匹，善明欲取之。

translations.literal: A merchant knew they were cheap and offered Rou thirty bolts; Shanming wanted to accept.
translations.idiomatic: A merchant knew they were cheap and offered thirty bolts; Shanming wanted to accept.

sentences.zh: 柔曰：「與人交易，一言便定，豈可以利動心也。

translations.literal: Rou said, "In dealing with people one word fixes the bargain— how can profit move the heart?"
translations.idiomatic: Rou said, "In trade one word fixes the bargain— how can profit move the heart?"

translations.literal: He then sold to the first man.
translations.idiomatic: He sold to the first man.

translations.literal: Gentry and officials who heard it admired and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry who heard it admired and submitted.

translations.literal: His pushing sincerity and holding faith were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His sincerity and faith were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 隴西王源賀採佛經幽旨，作祗洹精舍圖偈六卷，柔為之注解，咸得理衷，為當時儁僧所欽味焉。

translations.literal: Wang Yuanhe of Longxi gathered the subtle intent of Buddhist sutras and composed six juan of verse for the Jetavana Hermitage diagram; Rou annotated them and all attained principle at the center, admired by eminent monks of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanhe of Longxi composed six juan of Jetavana verses; Rou annotated them to the admiration of eminent monks.

translations.literal: He also composed inscriptions and eulogies that circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, He also composed inscriptions and eulogies that circulated in the world.

translations.literal: His son Mo, courtesy name Chongming.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mo, whose courtesy name was Chongming.

translations.literal: Administrator of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: He was Administrator of Wuwei.

translations.literal: Suo Chang, courtesy name Juzhen, was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Chang, whose courtesy name was Juzhen, came from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 為劉昞助教，專心經籍，盡能傳昞之業。

translations.literal: He was Liu Bing's assistant teacher and devoted himself to the classics, fully able to transmit Bing's enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: He was Liu Bing's assistant teacher, devoted to the classics, fully transmitting Bing's enterprise.

sentences.zh: 涼州平，入國，以儒學見拔，為中書博士。

translations.literal: When Liang Province was pacified he entered the state and was selected for Confucian learning as a Secretariat Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Province was pacified he entered the state and was made Secretariat Erudite for his learning.

translations.literal: Earnest and diligent in instruction, stern yet with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Earnest in instruction, stern yet courteous.

sentences.zh: 京師大族貴遊之子，皆敬憚威嚴，多所成益，前後顯達，位至尚書牧守者數十人，皆受業於敞。

translations.literal: Sons of great clans and noble travelers in the capital all feared his awesomeness and severity and gained much from him; dozens who reached Secretariat directors and governors had all studied under Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of great clans feared his severity and gained much; dozens who became directors and governors had studied under Chang.

translations.literal: Chang lectured for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: chang lectured for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 敞以喪服散在眾篇，遂撰比為喪服要記。

translations.literal: Chang, because mourning garments were scattered through many chapters, compiled a comparative Essentials of Mourning Garments.
translations.idiomatic: Because mourning garments were scattered through many texts, Chang compiled Essentials of Mourning Garments.

translations.literal: Many of his names, titles, and essays are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, Many of his names, titles, and essays are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 後出補扶風太守，在位清貧，未幾卒官。

translations.literal: Later he went out as Administrator of Fufeng; in office he was pure and poor and soon died in post.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went out as Administrator of Fufeng; pure and poor in office, he soon died.

sentences.zh: 時舊同學生等為請，[7]詔贈平南將軍、涼州刺史，諡曰獻。

translations.literal: Old fellow students and others petitioned for him [7]; an edict posthumously made him General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Liang Province, posthumous title Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Old students petitioned [7]; an edict posthumously made him General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Liang, posthumous title Xian.

sentences.zh: 敞子僧養，中書議郎、京兆太守。

translations.literal: Chang's son Sengyang was Secretariat Discussion Gentleman and Administrator of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: chang's son Sengyang was Secretariat Discussion Gentleman and Administrator of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 僧養子演貴，征東府參軍。

translations.literal: Sengyang's son Yangui was staff officer in the Pacify-the-East headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: sengyang's son Yangui was staff officer in the Pacify-the-East headquarters.

translations.literal: Yangui's son Huaizhen, courtesy name Gongdao.
translations.idiomatic: Yangui's son Huaizhen, whose courtesy name was Gongdao.

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the end of Wuding he was Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 初，敞在州之日，與鄉人陰世隆文才相友。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Chang was in the province, he and his townsman Yin Shilong were friends in literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in the province he and townsman Yin Shilong were friends in literary talent.

sentences.zh: 世隆至京師，被罪徙和龍，屆上谷，困不前達，土人徐能抑掠為奴。

translations.literal: Shilong reached the capital, was condemned and exiled to Helong; at Shanggu he was stranded and unable to advance; the local man Xu Neng seized and made him a slave.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong reached the capital, was exiled to Helong; at Shanggu Xu Neng made him a slave.

sentences.zh: 五年，敞因行至上谷，遇見世隆，語其由狀，對泣而別。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Chang on a journey reached Shanggu, met Shilong, heard his story, wept and parted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 Chang reached Shanggu, met Shilong, wept and parted.

translations.literal: Chang pleaded his case and he was freed.
translations.idiomatic: chang pleaded his case and he was freed.

sentences.zh: 世隆子孟貴，性至孝，每向田耘耨，早朝拜父，來亦如之。

translations.literal: Shilong's son Menggui was utmost filial by nature; each time he went to hoe fields he bowed to his father in the morning before leaving and again on return.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong's son Menggui was utmost filial; each day he bowed to his father before leaving for the fields and on return.

translations.literal: Townsmen admired his devotion to parents.
translations.idiomatic: townsmen admired his devotion to parents.

translations.literal: Yin Zhongda, a man of Guzang in Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongda came from Guzang in Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 祖訓，字處道，仕李暠為武威太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xun, courtesy name Chudao, served Li Gao as Administrator of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xun, whose courtesy name was Chudao, served Li Gao as Administrator of Wuwei.

translations.literal: His father Hua, courtesy name Jiwen, was Magistrate of Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hua, whose courtesy name was Jiwen, was Magistrate of Guzang.

translations.literal: Zhongda from youth was known for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: zhongda from youth was known for literary learning.

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu pacified Liang Province he was moved inward to the capital of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu pacified Liang Province he was moved to the capital of Dai.

sentences.zh: 司徒崔浩啟仲達與段承根云，二人俱涼土才華，同修國史。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Cui Hao memorialized that Zhongda and Duan Chenggen, both talents of the Liang region, should together revise the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao memorialized that Zhongda and Duan Chenggen, both Liang talents, should together revise the national history.

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretariat Drafting Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He served as appointed Secretariat Drafting Gentleman.

translations.literal: At his death.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 華次子周達，徐州平南司馬、太山太守。

translations.literal: Hua's second son Zhouda was staff officer in the Pacify-the-South headquarters of Xu Province and Administrator of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Hua's second son Zhouda was Pacify-the-South staff officer of Xu Province and Administrator of Taishan.

translations.literal: Zhouda's son Zunhe, childhood name Tiger Head.
translations.idiomatic: zhouda's son Zunhe, childhood name Tiger Head.

translations.literal: He loved music and valued martial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, He loved music and valued martial affairs.

sentences.zh: 初為高祖挽郎，拜奉朝請，後廣平王懷取為國常侍。

translations.literal: At first he was a dirge officer for Emperor Gaozu, appointed Court Attendant, later taken by Prince Huai of Guangping as regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was a dirge officer for Emperor Gaozu, then Court Attendant; Prince Huai of Guangping took him as regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 遵和便辟善事人，深為懷所親愛。

translations.literal: Zunhe was facile and good at pleasing people, deeply loved by Huai.
translations.idiomatic: zunhe was facile and good at pleasing people, deeply loved by Huai.

sentences.zh: 轉司空法曹、太尉中兵參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to law officer of the Minister of Works and middle army staff officer of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to law officer of the Minister of Works and Grand Marshal middle army staff officer.

sentences.zh: 又為汝南王悅郎中令，復被愛信。

translations.literal: Again he was made Director of the Palace Bureau to Prince Yue of Runan and again was loved and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Again he was Director of the Palace Bureau to Prince Yue of Runan and again loved and trusted.

sentences.zh: 稍遷龍驤將軍、驍騎將軍、豫州都督，鎮懸瓠。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred General of the Dragon, General of Valiant Cavalry, and Overseer of Yu Province, garrisoning Xuanchi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made General of the Dragon, General of Valiant Cavalry, and Overseer of Yu Province, garrisoning Xuanchi.

sentences.zh: 孝莊末，除左將軍、行豫州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was made General of the Left and acting Governor of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the end of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was made General of the Left and acting Governor of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 時前行州事元崇禮被徵將還，既聞尒朱兆入洛，遂矯殺遵和，擅攝州任。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Chongli, who had been handling provincial affairs, was summoned to return; when he heard Erzhu Rong had entered Luoyang, Zunhe falsely killed Chongli and usurped provincial authority.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chongli, then handling provincial affairs, was summoned back; hearing Erzhu Rong had entered Luoyang, Zunhe falsely killed Chongli and seized the province.

sentences.zh: 後追贈平南將軍、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously awarded General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 遵和兄子道方，性和雅，頗涉書傳，深為李神儁所知賞。

translations.literal: Zunhe's elder brother's son Daofang was mild and refined by nature, had read somewhat in books and histories, and was deeply known and admired by Li Shenjun.
translations.idiomatic: Zunhe's nephew Daofang was mild and refined, had read in books and histories, and was deeply admired by Li Shenjun.

sentences.zh: 神儁為前將軍、荊州刺史，請道方為其府長流參軍。

translations.literal: Shenjun was Forward General and Governor of Jing Province and requested Daofang as chief flowing clerk in his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjun was Forward General and Governor of Jing and took Daofang as chief flowing clerk.

sentences.zh: 神儁曾使道方詣蕭衍雍州刺史蕭綱論邊事，道方風神沉正，為綱所稱。

translations.literal: Shenjun once sent Daofang to Prince Gang of Xiao Yan, Governor of Yong Province, to discuss frontier affairs; Daofang's bearing was grave and correct and Gang praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjun sent Daofang to Prince Gang of Liang to discuss the frontier; Daofang's bearing was grave and correct and Gang praised him.

sentences.zh: 正光末，蕭綱遣其軍主曹義宗等擾動邊蠻，神儁令道方馳傳向新野，處分軍事。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengguang Prince Gang sent his army commander Cao Yizong and others to stir the frontier barbarians; Shenjun ordered Daofang to ride post-horses to Xinye to handle military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhengguang Prince Gang sent Cao Yizong to stir frontier tribes; Shenjun ordered Daofang to Xinye to handle military affairs.

sentences.zh: 於路為土因村蠻所掠，送於義宗，義宗又傳致襄陽，仍送於蕭衍，囚之尚方。

translations.literal: On the road he was plundered by barbarians of Tuyin village, sent to Yizong, Yizong passed him to Xiangyang, then sent him to Xiao Yan and imprisoned him in the Imperial Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he was seized by Tuyin village barbarians, sent to Yizong, then to Xiangyang and Xiao Yan, and imprisoned in the Imperial Workshop.

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang reign he was at last able to return to the state.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang he was at last able to return.

sentences.zh: 既至，拜奉朝請，轉員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Once he arrived he was appointed Court Attendant and transferred to Outer Court Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was appointed Court Attendant and Outer Court Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，遷尚書左民郎中，修起居注。

translations.literal: In the early Xiaozhuang reign he was transferred Secretariat Left People Section Gentleman and revised the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: In early Xiaozhuang he was Secretariat Left People Gentleman and revised the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，詔道方與儀曹郎中王元旭使於蕭衍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongan an edict sent Daofang with Wang Yuanxu of the Rites Section as envoys to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongan 2 an edict sent Daofang with Wang Yuanxu as envoys to Xiao Yan.

translations.literal: When they reached southern Yan Province there was an edict recalling them.
translations.idiomatic: At southern Yan Province an edict recalled them.

sentences.zh: 轉安東將軍、光祿大夫，領右民郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, concurrently Right People Section Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, concurrently Right People Gentleman.

translations.literal: In the early Taichang reign he died at forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In early Taichang he died at forty-two.

translations.literal: Gentlemen all sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: Men of standing all sighed in regret.

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：趙逸等皆通涉經史，才志不羣，價重西州，有聞東國，故於流播之中，拔泥滓之上。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Zhao Yi and the others all ranged through the classics and histories, talent and aim not of the common herd; their price was heavy in the western provinces and their fame reached the eastern states— therefore amid the scattering of exile they were lifted from the mud and mire.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Zhao Yi and the others all mastered classics and histories, with uncommon talent and aims; prized in the west and known in the east— amid exile they were lifted from the mud.

translations.literal: That a man cannot be without ability— it is true.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, That a man cannot be without ability— it is true.

sentences.zh: 胡叟顯晦之間，優遊無悶，亦一世之異人乎？

translations.literal: Hu Sou between obscurity and brightness wandered without care— was he not also a man apart in his age?
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sou, between obscurity and brightness, wandered without care— was he not a man apart in his age?

translations.idiomatic: collation notes

sentences.zh: 於郯城借假節以為軍威 張森楷云：「『假』當作『遐』。

translations.literal: At Tancheng he borrowed a false staff to restore military prestige: Zhang Senkai says: " 'False' should read 'Xia'."
translations.idiomatic: On borrowing a false staff at Tancheng for military prestige: Zhang Senkai says " 'False' should read 'Xia'."

sentences.zh: 上云『以遐持節、假平東將軍』，則假者將軍，非假節也。

translations.literal: Above it says "Xia with Bearer of the Staff, acting General Who Pacifies the East"— the "acting" applies to the general, not to the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Above it says Xia held Bearer of the Staff as acting General Who Pacifies the East— "acting" modifies the general, not the staff.

translations.literal: " According to Zhang's view this is correct; Comprehensive Mirror juan 147
translations.idiomatic: Zhang is correct; Comprehensive Mirror juan 147

translations.literal: 〈page 4599〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈page 4599〉

sentences.zh: 作「借趙遐節以為軍威」，即用此傳語，僅加一「趙」字，則司馬光所見魏書正作「遐」。

translations.literal: reads "borrowed Zhao Xia's staff for military prestige," using this biography's wording with only the addition of "Zhao"— thus what Sima Guang saw in the Book of Wei read "Xia."
translations.idiomatic: reads "borrowed Zhao Xia's staff for military prestige," using this passage with only "Zhao" added— thus Sima Guang's Book of Wei had "Xia."

sentences.zh: 河東裴定宗等謂潛曰 諸本「河」作「江」，北史卷三四胡叟傳作「河」。

translations.literal: Pei Dingzong of Hedong and others said to Qian: All editions read "river" for "He"; Northern History juan 34, Hu Sou biography reads "He."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Dingzong of Hedong said to Qian: editions read "river" for "He"; Northern History juan 34 reads "He."

sentences.zh: 按裴氏是河東大姓，「江」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: The Pei clan is a great surname of Hedong; "river" is erroneous and is now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The Pei are a great Hedong clan; "river" is an error, corrected here.

sentences.zh: 如彼在泉臨深是懼 按「泉」本當作「淵」，用詩「如臨深淵」語，當是唐人避諱追改。

translations.literal: Like one beside the spring, in deep places he fears: "Spring" should read "abyss," from the Odes "as if beside a deep abyss"— likely altered to avoid Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: "Spring" should be "abyss," from the Odes "as if beside a deep abyss"— likely a Tang taboo alteration.

sentences.zh: 下宗欽傳，欽與高允書「若夫泉江相忘之談」，「泉」亦當是「淵」字諱改。

translations.literal: Below in Zong Qin's biography, Qin's letter to Gao Yun "the talk of forgetting each other like the Spring and River"— "spring" there should also be "abyss" altered for taboo.
translations.idiomatic: In Zong Qin's letter to Gao Yun, "forgetting each other like the Spring and River"— "spring" should likewise be "abyss" under taboo.

sentences.zh: 無忘歲寒 殿本考證云：「詩凡十三章，此句下應如前注『其十三』三字。」

translations.literal: Do not forget the year's cold: The Palace Edition notes: "The poem has thirteen chapters; below this line there should be a note 'thirteen' as before."
translations.idiomatic: Do not forget the year's cold: Palace Edition notes the poem has thirteen chapters and a "thirteen" tag should appear here as before.

sentences.zh: 至涼州西四百里韭谷窟 百衲本「韭」作「［上非下灬］」，諸本作「韭」，北史卷三四劉延明傳作「韮」。

translations.literal: Four hundred li west of Liang Province at Jiugu Cave: the Palace Edition reads "leek" as a variant form; all editions "leek"; Northern History juan 34, Liu Yanming biography reads the same character in alternate form.
translations.idiomatic: Four hundred li west of Liang Province at Jiugu (Leek) Gorge: the Palace Edition has a variant graph; standard editions and Northern History juan 34 (Liu Yanming) use the leek-gorge character.

sentences.zh: 諸本此字下並有注云：「本或作『悲』，亦作『匪』。

translations.literal: All editions under this character have a note: "Some texts read 'grief' or 'not.'"
translations.idiomatic: Editions note: "Some texts read grief or not."

sentences.zh: 」按晉書卷九四郭瑀傳云：「隱於臨松薤谷，鑿石窟而居。

translations.literal: Jin History juan 94, Guo Yu biography says: "He hid at Linsong Xiangu, dwelling in a stone cave."
translations.idiomatic: Jin History juan 94, Guo Yu: "He hid at Linsong Xiangu in a stone cave."

sentences.zh: 」「薤」即「韭」「韮」，臨松在涼州西，敦煌東，劉昞死地當即郭瑀隱居之處。

translations.literal: "Xiangu" is "韭/韮"; Linsong is west of Liang and east of Dunhuang— Liu Bing's place of death should be where Guo Yu hid.
translations.idiomatic: "Xiangu" is leek-gorge; Linsong lies west of Liang— Liu Bing's death place should be Guo Yu's retreat.

sentences.zh: 「［上非下灬］」字不見字書，他本作「悲」或「匪」均「韭」字訛，今從諸本。

translations.literal: The variant character is not in dictionaries; other readings "grief" or "not" are all corruptions of the leek character— we follow the standard editions.
translations.idiomatic: The variant graph is not in dictionaries; readings "grief" or "not" are corruptions of the leek-gorge character— we follow the standard editions.

sentences.zh: 臣忝職史教 諸本「教」作「敢」，獨百衲本作「教」。

translations.literal: Your servant shamed in the post of history instruction: All editions read "dare" for "instruction"; only the Palace Edition reads "instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Shamed in the post of history instruction: editions read dare; only Palace Edition reads instruction.

sentences.zh: 李慈銘云：「當從宋本，以『教』字讀句，時光以司徒領著作，故曰『史教』。

translations.literal: Li Ciming says: "One should follow the Song edition, reading 'instruction' to close the clause— at the time Guang held the Secretariat and also the Drafting Office, hence 'history instruction.'"
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming: follow the Song edition— Guang held the Secretariat and Drafting Office, hence "history instruction."

sentences.zh: 」按李說是，若作「敢」，屬下讀，上云「臣忝職史」，語氣不完。

translations.literal: If it read "dare," it belongs to the following clause; above "your servant shamed in the post of history" the sense is incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: If "dare," it belongs below and the clause above is incomplete.

translations.literal: We now follow the Palace Edition.
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, We now follow the Palace Edition.

sentences.zh: 時舊同學生等為請 北史卷三四索敞傳「請」下有「諡」字，疑此傳脫去。

translations.literal: Old fellow students petitioned for him: Northern History juan 34, Suo Chang biography has "posthumous title" under "petition"— this biography may have dropped it.
translations.idiomatic: Old students petitioned: Northern History juan 34 Suo Chang adds "posthumous title" after petition— possibly dropped here.
